rationale: This is an explicitly acknowledged cosmetic re-parameterization of the archive winner `profitable_capex_own_history_low` (same profitability gate, same own-history capex-intensity leg, only TS_RANK swapped for a current/MA5 ratio), so it tests measurement resolution rather than any new economic content and will be near-collinear with the existing signal.

Fully firm-demeaning both legs is a coherent and internally consistent response to the diagnosed style-absorption problem, though it overlaps materially with the gen-0 `margin_up_capex_down_trend` (profit rising while capex falls) and differs mainly in using own-mean deviations and a product instead of trends and a difference, so incremental information is uncertain.

Net debt issuance scaled by cash flow is a direct restatement of the well-documented net-debt-issuance/external-financing anomaly and largely duplicates the archive's `outside_capital_per_internal_dollar` (which already put DELTA(dltt) over max(oancf,dp) with a profitability gate and produced t=0.43 alpha), so it is a rediscovery on two fronts.

Acquirer underperformance and the acquisition component of asset growth are established published anomalies, and because aqc is zero for most firm-years the RANK leg collapses to a near-binary acquirer indicator with a massive tie block, making the "conditional" interaction effectively a profitability sort within non-acquirers.

Pairing an SG&A-intensity change with own-norm capex restraint is a genuinely new construct that avoids the RMW-loading level gate, but the sign is not obviously safe — a falling SG&A/sales ratio is mechanically produced by sales growth and is elsewhere read as underinvestment in intangibles — so the expected positive sign rests on a contestable premise.

Normalizing capex intensity by its own five-year maximum is a near-monotone transform of the archive winner's TS_RANK leg and is also highly redundant with proposal 1 in this same batch, so it cannot cleanly discriminate among own-history benchmarks and adds little beyond a third parameterization of an already-tested mechanism.
